questions.question: What is the proper footwear for riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy footwear that covers and supports your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on things. Tuck in your laces so they don't get caught on anything.

questions.question: What does swerving a motorcycle require?

options.text: You should swerve to avoid hazards on slippery roads.

questions.explanation: Swerving is a quick move that needs a lot of traction to do safely. Avoid making sudden moves like swerving on wet or slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, what should you usually do?

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is dangerous when wet. When it rains, ride in the tire tracks left by cars to stay away from the center. The left tire track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: A friend has been drinking and wants to drive. Which should you NOT do?

options.text: Ask other friends to talk them out of driving.
Arrange a different way for them to get home.
Tell them to use less-crowded roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to use less-crowded roads.
questions.explanation: To stop someone from driving drunk, you can arrange other transportation, involve them in activities to slow their drinking, find reasons to keep them from leaving before they sober up, and ask other friends to help stop them.

questions.question: Which is NOT a cause of wobbling on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Most wobbles come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not try to speed up to stop a wobble.

questions.question: A vehicle is passing you on your left. What should you do?

options.text: Move as far to the right as possible to help them.
Move to the shoulder to help them.
Stay in the center portion of your lane.
Move to the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding too far right increases crash risk. Riding too far left may make them merge back too soon. Stay centered.

questions.question: Because motorcycles are small, they seem to be:

options.text: Going faster than they actually are.
Going slower than they actually are.
Not moving when they actually are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Going faster than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Because of their small size, motorcycles may look like they are going faster than they really are.

questions.question: Where should a child passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: They do not need to reach the footrests.

questions.explanation: A child passenger must sit right behind the operator. A child in front may not balance well and could get in the way of the controls.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of your lane should you use?

options.text: Either the left or right portion.

questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you away from opening doors, people stepping out, and cars pulling out.

questions.question: What happens to face shields and goggles over time?

options.text: They never need to be replaced.
They get scratches and become brittle, so they need regular replacement.
They should be made of breakable materials for crashes.
They should not let air pass through.

questions.correctAnswerText: They get scratches and become brittle, so they need regular replacement.
questions.explanation: Face shields and goggles are made of plastic. Over time, they get scratches and become brittle. Replace them regularly for the best protection and comfort.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes if you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip from car drippings. This strip is:

options.text: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny outside.
Always safe, no matter the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center of lanes. When the road is dry, this area gives enough grip for motorcycles. The oily strip is usually only two feet wide, so you can ride around it and stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: A dog is chasing your motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Go slow at first, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go slow at first, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog is chasing you, downshift and slow down. As you get closer, speed up and leave the dog behind.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, how should you turn your body?
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to see where you want to go. Turn only your head. Keep your shoulders still and your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about hazards or road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When entering a turn, a rider should:

options.text: Lean their shoulders to match the turn.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.explanation: Before turning, slow down by closing the throttle and using the brakes if needed.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders who do not wear helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries than riders who wear helmets.

questions.question: When following another vehicle, riding on the far side of the lane:

options.text: Is recommended because the driver will see you easily.
Is not recommended because drivers rarely check their side mirrors.
Is recommended because a passenger may tell the driver about you.
Is illegal because you must ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because drivers rarely check their side mirrors.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both actions at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve, but not both.
Only use the front brake and do not swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you need to brake and swerve, do them separately, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Do both at the same time.

questions.explanation: Do brake and swerve separately. Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake. Never do both at the same time.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips under five miles long at speeds under 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, it is best to:

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle. You may need to move from the outside of the curve to the inside before straightening out.

questions.question: As weight transfers to the front of your bike while braking, you should:

options.text: Gradually increase pressure to the front brake.
Not worry. Weight transfer will not affect your motorcycle.
Try to lock the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gradually increase pressure to the front brake.
questions.explanation: While braking, slowly increase the pressure on the front brake lever as the bike's weight moves forward to the front tire.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are usually rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the rear brake firmly while gradually increasing the braking pressure of the front brake.

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.
